title: Officers cleared in fatal shooting of machete-wielding man
article: Officers involved in the Oct. 23, 2010 shooting death of 28-year-old Amit Krishna of Parkdale will not face criminal charges.
Ian Scott, director of the province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU), announced his findings on Tuesday, March 29.

The SIU assigned five investigators and three forensic investigators to investigate the circumstances surrounding this case. Investigators took photographs and video recordings of the crime scene: an apartment unit at 200 Dufferin St., just south of King Street. They also took measurements and produced a scale drawing.

Investigators also seized five spent cartridge cases, a damaged projectile and a machete. The officers' service pistols were also confiscated for examination as were their uniforms and use of force options.
Further, the SIU interviewed several civilian witnesses in the building at the time of the shooting as well as several witness officers.

Police fatally shot Krishna when they went to the Parkdale residence to arrest him on an outstanding warrant, the SIU reported. One of the man's relatives allowed two police officers to enter the unit.

The officers approached the victim's bedroom, which was in complete darkness, locating Krishna under the covers of the bed. Police removed him from the bedroom and escorted him into the living room area explaining their reason for being there.

The officers then reportedly asked if Krishna wanted to wear different clothing before being taken into custody and followed the accused back into the bedroom. At this point, Krisna allegedly reached into a bag of clothing and pulled out a machete and lunged at the witness officer.
A struggle ensued and the SIU reported Krishna "landed a glancing blow with the machete to the left side of the witness officer's head." This is when the witness officer fired his gun at Krishna.
A post-mortem examination determined he sustained several fatal gunshot wounds.

"In my view, the subject officer was justified in the use of lethal force - he saw the witness officer in immediate jeopardy of grievous injury or death as a result of the knife attack by Mr. Krisna," Scott wrote in a March 29 statement.
"Accordingly, the subject officer was justified in responding with the use of his firearm, causing the death of Mr. Krishna."
The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates incidents involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.

The agency's director is charged with considering whether an officer has committed a criminal offence in connection with the incident under investigation; depending on the evidence, laying a criminal charge against the officer if appropriate or close the file without any charges being laid; and reporting the results of any investigators to the Attorney General.
